skill.name: ntm
skill.description: Named Tmux Manager orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini agents in tmux panes with dashboards, robot mode, work routing, and safety controls.
skill.summary: Coordinate multiple AI coding agents inside named tmux sessions.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples and inline command names. The audit confirms critical curl-to-bash installation instructions, persistent shell initialization, hidden prompt logging, outbound webhook support, and high-risk examples that disable agent safety controls.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash with package-manager installation, checksum verification, or a download-then-inspect flow.

remediation.issue: Shell integration appends eval output to ~/.zshrc.
remediation.suggestion: Document exactly what ntm init emits and ask users to review the generated shell snippet before adding it to startup files.

remediation.issue: Example agent commands disable permission and sandbox protections.
remediation.suggestion: Remove dangerous bypass flags from default examples and document them only as advanced, explicit opt-in options with warnings.

remediation.issue: Command hooks can run shell commands and log prompt content.
remediation.suggestion: Require clear warnings for hooks, avoid logging message bodies by default, and recommend least-privilege hook commands.

remediation.issue: Slack webhook notifications may send operational metadata externally.
remediation.suggestion: Document what payload fields are sent and advise users not to include secrets or sensitive prompts in webhook events.

content.value_statement: Managing several AI coding agents across terminals is hard to track. NTM provides tmux-based sessions, dashboards, routing, and automation for Claude Code, Codex, and related tools.
actual_capabilities: Creates named tmux sessions with multiple Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini panes.
Sends prompts to selected agents or all agents in a session.
Shows dashboards, status views, health checks, and pane output capture.
Provides robot-mode commands for scripted inspection, spawning, assignment, and replay.
Documents work triage, agent mail, checkpoint, hook, and notification workflows.
Includes safety checks intended to block dangerous commands from AI agents.
limitations: Requires tmux and the relevant agent CLIs to be installed and authenticated.
Many features depend on external Flywheel ecosystem tools such as BV, CASS, and Agent Mail.
Automation can be risky if hooks or agent commands are configured without safeguards.
The skill file is documentation only and does not include the Go CLI source code.

use_cases.title: Run parallel implementation tracks
use_cases.description: Create one tmux session with separate agents for architecture, implementation, testing, and review work.

use_cases.title: Monitor long-running agent sessions
use_cases.description: Use dashboards, activity views, health checks, and output capture to supervise several coding agents from one terminal.

use_cases.title: Automate agent coordination
use_cases.description: Use robot-mode commands to inspect sessions, assign work, replay prompts, and integrate with task automation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use NTM to create a tmux session for my project with two Claude Code agents and one Codex agent.

prompt_templates.title: Send work to agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Use NTM to send an implementation task to Claude agents and a test-writing task to Codex agents in the same session.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect session health
prompt_templates.prompt: Use NTM robot mode to summarize session health, context usage, recent output, and stalled panes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-agent workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an NTM workflow that assigns design, implementation, review, testing, and documentation across multiple agents with checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Show me the current agent session status.
output: A session summary with pane names, agent types, activity states, and context indicators.
A list of stalled or unhealthy panes that need attention.
A suggested split between architecture, implementation, tests, and review.
Commands or steps for sending each prompt to the right agent group.

output_examples.input: Capture all Claude pane output for review.
output_examples.output: A saved or copied transcript summary focused on the selected Claude panes.

best_practices: Review install scripts before execution and prefer package-manager installs when possible.
Keep agent permission and sandbox protections enabled unless you have a controlled environment.
Use clear session names and checkpoint before large multi-agent changes.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installers directly to a shell in sensitive environments.
Do not configure agents with unrestricted bypass flags for normal development work.
Do not log prompts or pane output to persistent files unless the data is safe to retain.

faq.question: What does NTM manage?
faq.answer: It manages named tmux sessions that contain multiple AI coding agents and related workflow panes.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The documentation describes support for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and Claude-compatible workflows.

faq.question: Can it send prompts to multiple agents?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents commands for sending prompts to Claude, Codex, Gemini, or all agents in a session.

faq.question: Does it include automation APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Robot mode provides machine-readable commands for status, context, spawning, assignment, and replay.

faq.question: Is it safe to install with the one-line installer?
faq.answer: The documented curl-to-bash installer is risky. Review the script or use a safer package installation method.

faq.question: What should I configure carefully?
faq.answer: Review shell hooks, webhook notifications, startup-file changes, and any agent command that disables approvals or sandboxing.
